name: RHI Magnesita India Limited
industry: Refractories (specialty industrial materials for steel, cement, glass, non-ferrous, foundry)

moat_sources.name: switching_costs
moat_sources.evidence_note: Refractory products require multi-year, plant-specific qualification/trial cycles before a steel or cement customer adopts them -- a genuine technical switching cost. But this is an industry-wide characteristic shared by every major player (Vesuvius India, IFGL Refractories, Tata Krosaki), not a demonstrated RHIM-specific advantage; no company-specific retention-rate or contract-tenure evidence was found in public sources.

moat_sources.name: intangible_assets
moat_sources.evidence_note: Public commentary (analyst notes, business press) states RHIM can source raw material and technology from its global parent RHI Magnesita N.V. (LSE-listed, world's largest refractories group), a genuine differentiator versus peers reliant on Chinese raw-material imports. This is a real structural angle (matches the global-parent technology-transfer thesis), but it is also a single-supplier dependency/related-party concentration risk, and margins have not shown a clear, sustained superiority over peers on the data found -- rated AMBER rather than GREEN pending harder evidence.

moat_sources.name: cost_advantage
moat_sources.evidence_note: No public evidence of a demonstrated, durable cost advantage versus peers was found. EBITDA margin has swung widely by year (roughly 10%-20% across FY22-FY26) driven by raw-material cost pass-through timing, not structural cost leadership, and two of the last five fiscal years produced a net loss (FY24 operating loss; FY26 impairment-driven loss) -- inconsistent with a strong, defensible cost moat.

moat_sources.name: pricing_power
moat_sources.evidence_note: No evidence of durable, independent pricing power: reported margins compress and recover in step with raw-material cost cycles rather than the company setting price ahead of input costs. Customers are large, concentrated steel/cement producers with real bargaining leverage in a fragmented multi-supplier market (RHIM ~25-30% share, Vesuvius India, IFGL Refractories, Tata Krosaki Refractories all present).

industry_context.phase_evidence: Refractories is an established, already-penetrated intermediate-industrial-goods category tightly linked to global/domestic steel and cement capacity utilization. India's steel output continues to grow (refractory demand is largely opex/tonnage-linked -- furnaces need relining on every production campaign, not only on new capex), which is a real long-run volume tailwind, but public commentary indicates RHIM's relative market share has been flat over the last six years while a smaller peer (IFGL) gained share and two larger peers (Vesuvius India, Tata Krosaki) lost share -- i.e. a fragmented, cyclical, share-stable market rather than an emergent or consolidating one. Classified MATURE rather than INFLECTION on the balance of evidence found.

bridge_assumptions.margin_delta_mechanism_note: Q1 FY26 showed EBITDA margin expanding ~370bps YoY (10.8% -> 14.5%) on cost actions and pricing, but this is a single quarter against a five-year history of margin volatility (roughly 10%-20% swings) and two net-loss years. Per the 6A rule, an unevidenced margin delta is set to zero here and the bridge is run purely on revenue-driven growth rather than assumed margin expansion.

variant_perception.market_belief: Market appears to price RHIM as a cyclical, customer-concentrated industrial supplier to steel/cement, currently de-rated after a large FY26 headline net loss (Rs -382.94 Cr, driven by a Rs 556-661 Cr non-cash goodwill/investment impairment) layered on an already-volatile earnings history (FY24 was also a net-loss year).
variant_perception.whats_wrong_with_belief: Attempted candidate thesis: the FY26 loss is a one-off non-cash impairment rather than an operating deterioration, and Q1 FY26 showed real operating improvement (EBITDA margin +370bps YoY, PAT nearly doubled). However this does not clear the bar for a credible, well-evidenced variant view: (a) it is only one quarter of confirming data: (b) on adjusted/normalized FY26 PAT (~Rs180 Cr, company-reported 'adjusted' basis) the stock's trailing PE is still roughly ~45-49x, i.e. the market is not obviously mispricing it even after looking through the impairment; and (c) there is no confirmed structural share-gain or margin-expansion trend to anchor a durable re-rating case.

JUDGEMENT CALLS: industry_context.phase set to MATURE (not INFLECTION) because, despite a genuine India-steel-output volume tailwind, no evidence of RHIM-specific share gain or profit-pool expansion was found (peer commentary says RHIM's relative share has been flat, not rising). moat_sources rated AMBER at best (switching costs, parent-relationship intangibles) and RED on pricing power/cost advantage, given repeated margin volatility and two net-loss years in five. variant_perception.answered is explicitly set to FALSE: a candidate 'market overreacts to a one-off non-cash impairment' thesis was tested and did not survive scrutiny (adjusted-earnings PE is still rich, and the operating-improvement evidence is a single quarter), so per the task's own instruction this is reported honestly as an unanswered N7 rather than an invented conviction call. m5_protocol_complete is set FALSE because this dossier was compiled solely from public web search under real tool/egress constraints, without primary-document review or an adversarial second pass.
